analysis: The only changed file is console-ui/package-lock.json, a lockfile-only dependency refresh. It bumps next from ^16.2.11 to ^16.4.2 and vitest from ^4.1.2 to ^5.0.5. It also bumps the @babel/* packages and moves sharp from 0.34.5 to 0.35.5, with libvips 1.3.4. Other changes are the @swc/helpers, ws (nested under @solana, 8.20.0 to 8.22.0) and @jridgewell/sourcemap-codec bumps. The @rolldown/binding-*, @oxc-project/types, @standard-schema/spec and several @vitest/* packages (expect, pretty-format, runner, snapshot) are removed. All new resolved URLs and integrity hashes point to registry.npmjs.org, and I saw no git, tarball, or non-registry sources. I found no integrity-hash removals. The consumer console is explicitly out of scope in the canonical threat model, which covers the provider, the native runtime and the provider/coordinator contract. Nothing in the diff touches any of those. It does not touch A-001 to A-017, TB-002, TB-003, TB-007, TB-009, TB-010 or TB-011, nor any of the T-xxx threats listed, and it changes no provider Swift code, attestation, App Attest, key or cache logic. The lockfile patch is truncated in the last unit (the range map is incomplete, ending around the @vitest/mocker entries), so later hunks were not visible. This is a coverage limit, not evidence of safety. Even so, the console is out of scope, so no integration follow-up on provider security is needed.
